description: The hour this row describes, in Coordinated Universal Time.
Electricity produced by natural-gas power plants across ERCOT this hour.
Electricity produced by coal power plants across ERCOT this hour.
Electricity produced by ERCOT's two nuclear plants (Comanche Peak and South Texas Project) this hour.
Electricity from smaller sources not broken out separately (biomass, landfill gas, etc.).
Electricity produced by solar farms across ERCOT this hour. Always 0 at night.
Electricity produced by hydroelectric plants. Very small in Texas.
Electricity produced by wind farms across ERCOT this hour.
Electricity used in the Coast weather zone (greater Houston).
Electricity used in the East weather zone (Tyler / Longview area).

plain_english_name: Demand - Far West Region / Permian Basin (MWh)
description: Electricity used in the Far West weather zone (Midland-Odessa / Permian Basin oil & gas country).

plain_english_name: Demand - North Central Region / Dallas-Fort Worth (MWh)
description: Electricity used in the North Central weather zone. This is our stand-in for the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex.
Electricity used in the North weather zone (Wichita Falls area).

plain_english_name: Demand - South Central Region / Austin-San Antonio (MWh)
description: Electricity used in the South Central weather zone (Austin / San Antonio).

plain_english_name: Demand - South Region / Rio Grande Valley (MWh)
description: Electricity used in the South weather zone (Corpus Christi / Rio Grande Valley).
Electricity used in the West weather zone (Abilene / San Angelo).
Electricity ERCOT sent to (+) or received from (-) Mexico's grid (CFE/CENACE) this hour.
Sum of every fuel type - the total amount of electricity ERCOT produced this hour.
Net electricity ERCOT sent to (+) or received from (-) all neighboring grids combined.
Total electricity used across all of ERCOT (the whole state) this hour.

plain_english_name: Power Traded with Southwest Power Pool (MWh)
description: Electricity ERCOT sent to (+) or received from (-) the Southwest Power Pool (a neighboring U.S. grid) this hour.
What ERCOT predicted total demand would be for this hour, published the day before.
Flags the ~2,644 hours whose original timestamp had a data error that we fixed during cleaning.
The same hour as the UTC timestamp, converted to Texas local time (handles daylight saving automatically).
Calendar year, local time.
Calendar month, local time.
The hour of day in Texas time; 0 = midnight, 17 = 5 PM.
Day of the week as a number, local time.
1 if this hour falls on a Saturday or Sunday, local time.
Winter (Dec-Feb), Spring (Mar-May), Summer (Jun-Aug), or Fall (Sep-Nov).
Same value as North Central demand - repeated under a clearer name since DFW is our focus.

plain_english_name: DFW Share of Total Texas Demand
description: DFW demand divided by total Texas demand. 0.30 means DFW used 30% of all the electricity in Texas that hour.

plain_english_name: Total Renewable Generation - Wind + Solar + Hydro (MWh)
description: Wind, solar, and hydro generation added together.
Renewable generation divided by total demand. 0.42 means renewables covered 42% of that hour's demand.
Total demand minus wind and solar generation - the amount other power plants (mostly gas, coal, nuclear) had to cover.
How far off ERCOT's forecast was. Positive = ERCOT over-predicted demand; negative = under-predicted.
The size of the forecast miss as a percentage, ignoring direction. Smaller is better.
